name: The Blossomwood
subtitle: The Bell of Waking
author: Luminati
description: Chapter One of The Bells of Evermere: a spring wood under ice in the morning — the woodcutters' camp, the wayside chimes, the frozen falls, Rimehart's glade and the shrine of the Bell of Waking. Generated by tools/make-bells-of-evermere.mjs.

objects.name: The Keeper's Lodge
text: The lodge is shut. Frost has grown over the latch like a second lock.

objects.name: The Keeper's Lodge
text: Inside, a kettle is already on. Mother Yarrow did not waste a minute.

objects.name: Corin's Hut
text: A hut of split logs. Snares hang from every peg — and one rabbit, frozen in mid-escape.

objects.speaker: Signpost
text: The bridge went in the first winter. Mind the edge.

objects.name: The Woodshed
text: Cut logs, stacked to the rafters. Seven winters of firewood, and still the cold comes in.

objects.name: The Charcoal Burner's Hut
text: The charcoal burner's hut. His last fire is still laid in the hearth, seven years unlit.

objects.name: Mother Yarrow
objects.title: Keeper of the Shrine
talk: * Mother Yarrow: Seven years I sat in Evermere with my hands in my lap, listening for that bell. And then — there it was. Clear as morning. #line:86B0899198EEB58A980692EE944E6424
Mother Yarrow: Sit a moment. You've brought the spring up a hill; you can rest your legs. #line:B8360F956A4D40E37B2D211F71CA9865
* Mother Yarrow: The stag? It goes up into the high wood every spring and comes down every autumn. Seven years it stood still. Now it's late, and it knows it. #line:5F0B3236631FFABAA2EA2E8ECD53BE36
* Mother Yarrow: Your grandfather tuned the wayside chimes, you know. Wake, Turn, Gold. He said a wood should learn the song before the children did. #line:A9D958C695E55ABA805D2B36293954D8
